Marília Panitz, in her text “To What Matters, an Answer”, proposes an itinerary for reading Barja’s works based on the concept of the equation, so dear to the artist. In the “enigmas of visual equations” of Barja’s commentary-constructions, the author highlights the condensation of meanings whose tool is humour. Appropriating the sharp steel of irony, armed with a laughter of Oswaldian inspiration, the anthropophagous Barja, under a “strong influence of the neo-concrete movement”, composes a set of installations in which he makes reference, in the titles of his installations, to a series of artists fundamental to modern and contemporary art, such as “O Sol de Goethe”, “Pega Manet”, “São João Beuys”, “Ser ou não Ser. Ao Gullar”. Panitz identifies in these declarations “of ideological affiliation” singular, ambiguous, radical visions of the contemporary gaze. Visions that, in the 1990s, incorporated opacity and the re-elaboration of the very concept of gaze through the metaphor of blindness. In her suggestive itinerary, Panitz interweaves the hidden ribbons that bind together work
